title: Node multiplexing headroom playbook for private VPC sizing
body:
Purpose:
This working sheet is an operational playbook and quick calculator for applying node multiplexing and conservative headroom rules when sizing Private/VPC GPU deployments. Focus: reduce BOM cost and rack footprint while preserving latency SLOs and fault tolerance.

Status / context notes: Draft — derived from recent fleet experiments (Q3–Q4 2025) and procurement quotes. Not yet signed off by infra finance. Use with caution for customer proposals; run final numbers with procurement.

Key concepts (short):
- Node multiplexing: share a single GPU host across multiple low-concurrency LLM workloads by scheduling non-overlapping KV/sequence hot paths and leveraging software-isolated runtimes.
- Headroom: spare capacity buffer to absorb short-term traffic bursts and node failures without immediate fallback to higher-cost regions. Expressed as a percent of baseline required throughput.
- Safety spare: dedicated physical spare GPUs/hosts for rapid replacement vs. logical headroom for traffic absorb.

Assumptions used in these exercises (change as needed):
- Baseline model: 13B dense transformer (A200-equivalent perf when quantized int8)
- Effective tokens/sec per GPU under steady concurrent streaming: 1,200 tokens/s (quantized) on average workloads
- Average request length: 220 tokens (request+response), median tail P95 latency goal: < 350ms per request
- Multiplexing degradation factor: 0.85 (i.e., multiplexing adds 15% throughput overhead due to context-switch and isolation costs)
- Procurement SKU price (list): A200-class node: $24,000; NVLink-enabled 8xA800 rack node: $48,000; Switch/Top-of-Rack per rack $10,000; Rack + power + cooling per rack $12,000. (internal quotes needed for finalized pricing)

Operational knobs and formulas (copy into calculator cells):
1) Effective throughput per host (T_eff) = (base_tokens_per_sec * multiplex_factor) * quantization_gain.
   - base_tokens_per_sec (B) = 1200
   - multiplex_factor (M) = 1 - multiplex_overhead (e.g., 0.85 => overhead 0.15). So M = 0.85.
   - quantization_gain (Q) = 1.0 for int8 baseline; 1.25 if running model-specific INT4 path (experimental)

2) Concurrent requests capacity (R) = floor(T_eff * safety_window_seconds / avg_request_tokens)
   - safety_window_seconds = expected time window to clear outstanding tokens while meeting latency SLO (recommend 2.0s)

3) Required hosts (N) = ceil(projected_peak_tokens_per_sec / T_eff * (1 + provisioning_headroom_pct))
   - provisioning_headroom_pct = e.g., conservative: 30%, standard: 20%, aggressive: 10%

4) Safety spares per region: recommended = max(1, ceil(N * spare_ratio)) where spare_ratio = 0.03–0.07 depending on procurement lead time

Quick worked example (copy to cells and play):
- Customer peak concurrency requirement: 10,000 concurrent active requests at peak (expected weekly peak)
- avg_request_tokens = 220; safety_window = 2.0s -> tokens in-flight per concurrent request = 220/2=110 tokens/s equivalent per concurrent request? (we use tokens/sec framing below)
Compute projected_peak_tokens_per_sec = concurrent_reqs * avg_request_tokens / safety_window_seconds = 10000 * 220 / 2 = 1,100,000 tokens/s
T_eff = B * M * Q = 1200 * 0.85 * 1.0 = 1,020 tokens/s per host
N_raw = 1,100,000 / 1,020 = 1,078.43 -> N = ceil(1078.43 * (1 + 0.30)) = ceil(1402.0) = 1402 hosts
Safety spares (spare_ratio 0.05) = max(1, ceil(1402 * 0.05)) = 71 hosts spare (logical / can be cold power-off)

BOM sketch and procurement grouping (rack-oriented):
- Hosts per rack (standard): 10 (varies by node size and power).
- Racks needed = ceil((N + spares)/hosts_per_rack) = ceil((1402+71)/10) = 148 racks
- Hardware line items (rough):
  * GPU hosts: 1,473 x A200-class (~$24k ea) -> subtotal hosts $35.4M
  * Network: 148 x ToR ($10k) -> $1.48M
  * Rack infra (PDUs, rails, cooling margin): 148 x $12k -> $1.78M
  * Contingency / spares: we baked in spares above but include 7% procurement buffer -> ~$2.6M
  * Total rough capex estimate: ~$41.2M (very rough)

Notes on multiplexing sizing sensitivity:
- If multiplexing overhead is higher (M=0.75) or traffic exhibits high simultaneous peak tails, the host count increases nonlinearly. Retain scenario table in calculator: M = [0.7,0.8,0.85,0.9,1.0].
- Quantization delta: Q = [1.0,1.12,1.25]. Q depends on model fidelity/regressions — always verify with the eval suite (redwood Optimize).

Regional tiling and cross-region headroom:
- Rule of thumb: keep at least 20% of region capacity as cross-region failover reserved (not counted in local headroom). For enterprise customers with strict locality, prefer extra spares in-region.
- Multi-AZ distribution per region: spread hosts across >=3 AZs when possible to avoid AZ-sized outages; map racks to AZs in contiguous increments not to exceed rack power or networking constraints.

Failure and recovery model:
- Mean time to replace (MTTR) assumptions: hot-swap replaceable hosts ~ 4 hours (with on-call ops); if procurement spares not available, fallback to cross-region burst -> latency/regression risk.
- If one rack fails (10 hosts), absorbed by headroom = headroom_percent * active_capacity. Use simulation to ensure headroom > 1 rack for common rack-failure scenarios.

Checklist for running final proposal (TODO):
- [ ] Replace SKU pricing with current procurement quotes (Procure Q4 2025 spreadsheet id: PRC-2025-11)
- [ ] Validate multiplexing factor with workload-specific microbench (bench harness ID: bench/multiplex-2025)
- [ ] Run 5 worst-case tail prompts through degrade/regression evals (link to redwood Optimize eval set)
- [ ] Align rack electrical load plan with DC vendor (rack amp draw / PDUs)
- [ ] Legal review for international shipment/regulatory items if region = EU/APAC

Practical notes & pitfalls (observations from past projects):
- Multiplexing helps most for chatty low-token-turn workloads; for long-generation batch participants, multiplexing yields less advantage.
- KV cache locality matters: when sharing hosts across models with very different token prefix reuse, cache churn can kill throughput. Prefer grouping similar models per multiplexed pool.
- Conservative headroom (30%) recommended for first deployment; once SLA are proven, move to 15–20% operational headroom and increase cold-spare pool for hardware replacement instead.
